small_guidance:
- Swap the loop order to be over output channels in the inner-most position with a register accumulator vector of size C_OUT (or tile of OC) so input/weight loads for each (kh,kw,ic) are reused across all OC — currently each input pixel is reloaded 64× (once per oc).
- Increase BLOCK_SP to 256 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3; the spatial tile is the coalesced dim and a wider tile amortizes the weight broadcast loads.
- Cache weights for a given (ic,kh,kw) in a scalar register and broadcast across the BLOCK_SP vector; hoist `(pid_n * C_IN + ic) * H_IN` out of the kh/kw loops.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a fused conv→min kernel where each program computes a spatial tile for one batch and accumulates ALL OC outputs simultaneously in registers (OC=64 fits easily as a [BLOCK_SP, 64] or 64 separate [BLOCK_SP] accumulators). Loop order: for ic, for kh, for kw: load x tile once, then for oc: FMA into acc[oc]. This reduces input-tile loads by 64× and is the dominant bottleneck.
- After the conv loop, reduce min across the 64 accumulators in-register (tree of tl.minimum), apply tanh(tanh(.)) on the scalar-per-pixel result, and store — single pass, no intermediate NCHW conv tensor written.
- Consider channels_last input layout (NHWC) so the IC loop becomes a contiguous gather; with C_IN=16 and KH*KW=9, an im2col-style [BLOCK_SP, 144] × [144, 64] tiny GEMM via tl.dot is also viable on Ampere/Ada tensor cores and would massively beat the current scalar-FMA loop.
